'''Darington Hobson''' (born September 29, 1987) is an American college basketball player formerly for the [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball]] team. Born in [[Las Vegas metropolitan area|Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], Hobson attended five high schools and a junior college before finally becoming eligible to play college basketball. 

== High school and junior college ==
Hobson attended Western High School in Las Vegas for his freshmen year <ref name="multiple">{{cite web|url=http://www.golobos.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hobson_darington00.html |title=Player Bio: Darington Hobson – NEW MEXICO OFFICIAL ATHLETIC SITE |publisher=Golobos.com |date=September 29, 1987 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}}</ref>, before moving to Houston, Texas to attend Alief Hastings High School. At fifteen he attended Gulf Shores Academy <ref name="multiple"/>, earning his nickname of "Butta" through his pick-up play in Houston <ref name="multiple2">{{cite web|last=Leung |first=Diamond |url=http://espn.go.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/7120/only-a-matter-of-time-for-hobson |title=Only a 'matter of time' for Hobson – College Basketball Nation Blog – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=March 16, 2010 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}}</ref>. He then moved to southern California and attended his fourth high school of  Calvary Baptist Christian. Eventually, he finally moved to Decatur Christian in Illinois for prep school <ref name="multiple3">{{cite web|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/cbk/story/Goodman-New-Mexico-Hobson-010610# |title=Hobson making his mark after long road to New Mexico – CBK News – FOX Sports on MSN |publisher=Msn.foxsports.com |date=January 7, 2010 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}}</ref>. At Decatur Christian, Hobson was prompted by his coach, Alan Huss, to take the ACT, where he passed <ref name="multiple3"/>. Hobson, rated a 4-star recruit by Scout.com, was coming off a season where he averaged 19 points, 12 rebounds and 7 assists <ref name="multiple"/>. He still needed credit, and therefore attended the [[College of Eastern Utah]], leading them to a 25–7 record where he averaged 15.2 points and 8.7 rebounds.

== University of New Mexico ==
===Junior Year, 2009-2010===

Upon coming to UNM, Hobson broke down and cried. "You always wished that you were there and playing on that level," Hobson said. "When I finally got there, I just sat in my room and just thanked God and cried for a couple of hours because I finally got to the place where I always wanted to get."<ref name="multiple2">{{cite web|last=Leung |first=Diamond |url=http://espn.go.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/7120/only-a-matter-of-time-for-hobson |title=Only a 'matter of time' for Hobson – College Basketball Nation Blog – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=March 16, 2010 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}}</ref> 

Virtually unknown coming into the season, the left-handed Hobson was the question mark in how successful UNM's season would be. The Lobos had players in Roman Martinez and [[Dairese Gary]], but the 6'7" [[point forward]] JC transfer Hobson was the key to the year where the Lobos were picked fifth in the [[Mountain West Conference]]. He did not disappoint, being the first Lobo to ever lead the team in points, rebounds and assists in the regular season. In 2010, Hobson was awarded the [[Mountain West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] and Newcomer of the Year, making him the only player to ever achieve both honors in the same year <ref name="multiple4">{{cite web|url=http://www.themwc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030810aac.html |title=Mountain West Conference Announces 2009–10 Men's Basketball All-Conference Awards – MWC OFFICIAL ATHLETIC SITE |publisher=Themwc.com |date=March 8, 2010 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}}</ref>. He was also named to First-Team All-Mountain West <ref name="multiple4">{{cite web|url=http://www.themwc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030810aac.html |title=Mountain West Conference Announces 2009–10 Men's Basketball All-Conference Awards – MWC OFFICIAL ATHLETIC SITE |publisher=Themwc.com |date=March 8, 2010 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}}</ref>. He was also one of twenty-six finalists for the [[John R. Wooden Award]], which annually awards the most outstanding player in men's college basketball <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.woodenaward.com/?cat=3 |title=Top Candidates – Men – Wooden Award |publisher=Woodenaward.com |date= |accessdate=March 22, 2010}}</ref>. On March 29, 2010, Hobson was named an Associated Press Third Team All-American, the first since [[Danny Granger]] in 2005 <ref>http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=5037799</ref>

Hobson had 30 points and 10 rebounds against Louisiana Tech on November 21, 2009, going 3 for 4 from behing the arc. He had 22 points and 15 rebounds against the California on December 2, 2009, only to best that with a 29-point, 12-rebound performance against San Diego St. on February 2, including a 56-footer at the first half buzzer <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=llvdHvVhhcM |title=Lobos Darrington Hobson with halftime buzzer beater |publisher=YouTube |date= |accessdate=March 22, 2010}}</ref>. On February 23, Hobson was two points away from being only the second Lobo in UNM history to record a triple-double, with 8 points, 10 rebounds and 11 assists. In the [[2010 Mountain West Conference Men's Basketball Tournament]], Hobson had 28 points and 15 rebounds en route to a 75–69 Lobos victory over the Air Force Academy.

On April 15, 2010, after declaring his eligibility for the NBA draft, Hobson was challenged in a one-on-one dunk contest with St. Pius X High School senior Kaelan Brennan at St. Pius's Lobo Day. While both contestants shot relatively poorly, both Hobson did show his surprise in the competition.<ref>http://espn.go.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/tag/_/name/darington-hobson</ref>[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kQQs2rOMdGQ&feature=player_embedded]

== NBA Career ==
===Draft===
On April 13, 2010, it was reported that Hobson declared himself eligible for the NBA Draft while not hiring an agent, leaving the possibility of returning to college basketball a possibility <ref>http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2010/news/story?id=5079573</ref>. On May 8, 2010, Hobson declared for the [[2010 NBA Draft]], forfeiting his final year of eligibility at the University of New Mexico.<ref>http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=5172555</ref>
